Is this same-entity with spelling/legal-suffix drift? Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH vs Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG. These are actually two different legal entities in the Sartorius group. Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG is the actual operating company of the Sartorius Lab division (the group renamed/restructured: Sartorius AG split into Sartorius AG and Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG around 2018). "Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH" was an older entity name (Goettingen). They're genuinely distinct legal names. The certificate document is the legal instrument, and the certificate says "Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG".

Rule: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is this "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift"? No — the core name differs: "Weighing Technology" vs "Lab Instruments". These are different divisions/companies within Sartorius group. Actually historically, Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH was renamed? Let me think. Sartorius Mechatronics... Sartorius AG renamed divisions: Sartorius Stedim Biotech (bioprocess) and Sartorius Lab Products & Services. In 2018 the German operating companies were restructured: Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG became the main operating company. Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH was a subsidiary in Göttingen handling weighing technology. They are distinct legal entities. The certificate (2018) issued to Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG.

So verdict: different-entity, best_value = document value: "Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG".

Why: The legal names differ beyond spelling/suffix drift (different operating companies within the Sartorius group), and the certificate is the authoritative legal instrument.
